en: The Question on the Characteristic of Wisdom (Paññā)
"Venerable Nāgasena, what is the characteristic of wisdom?
"Great King, I have already stated this before."
“Wisdom has the characteristic of cutting,” it was said; “but furthermore, wisdom has the characteristic of illuminating.
“How, venerable sir, does wisdom have the characteristic of illuminating?
“When wisdom arises, Great King, it dispels the darkness of ignorance, generates the light of true knowledge, reveals the radiance of understanding, and makes the Noble Truths manifest.”
“Then the practitioner of yoga sees with right wisdom: ‘It is impermanent,’ or ‘It is suffering,’ or ‘It is non-self.
“Just as if, O Great King, a man were to bring a lamp into a house in darkness; once brought in, the lamp dispels the darkness, produces radiance, reveals light, and makes visible forms manifest.”

"In the same way, Great King, when wisdom arises, it dispels the darkness of ignorance, generates the light of true knowledge, reveals the radiance of understanding, and makes the Noble Truths manifest.
Then the practitioner of yoga sees with right wisdom: ‘It is impermanent,’ or ‘It is suffering,’ or ‘It is non-self.
Thus, Great King, wisdom has the characteristic of illumination."
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, the Question on the Characteristic of Wisdom.
